key_insight: The paper targets a key bottleneck in ultra-long-context AI: finding which tokens deserve attention without an expensive search. Its title proposes Latent Sparse Attention as a route toward subquadratic attention, but the supplied abstract is truncated before the method and findings are described.
problem_solved: Above one million tokens, full attention becomes prohibitively expensive. Existing sparse-attention indexers can still require quadratic computation or lose accuracy at this scale.
method: Uses sparse attention as the framing: an indexer selects a subset of keys rather than attending to every token.
Proposes Latent Sparse Attention, targeting subquadratic scaling for ultra-long contexts.
The supplied excerpt does not specify the latent representation, indexing algorithm, or experimental results.
impact: More efficient ultra-long-context attention could support long-horizon agents and scientific workflows that need extensive context. Practical speedups and accuracy gains cannot be assessed from the supplied excerpt.
visual_elements: Token-grid comparison: dense all-to-all attention versus sparse selected connections.
Indexer pipeline: query → key selection → attention over selected keys, labeled as the general sparse-attention setup.
Conceptual scaling chart: quadratic cost versus a subquadratic target, clearly marked as illustrative rather than measured.
Long-context timeline exceeding one million tokens, with relevant passages highlighted.
paper_title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention
paper_authors: Ales Kubicek, Andrea Caciolai, Liangzu Peng, Sukrit Sumant, Benjamin Hoover
